L:
Dear Jo,
My husband and I have been together for twelve years, since college. We have good jobs, a nice apartment in Curitiba and a lazy cat. But lately everything feels mundane: work, dinner, TV, sleep, and the same again the next day. We're stuck in a rut.
Last month we finally had a heart to heart, and he asked me what I really wanted. I told him I had always dreamed of taking a three-month cooking course in Lisbon. He didn't get angry. He just asked if I wanted to go alone, and I said yes.
Now my sister says a break is one foot out the door. My friends keep asking whether we're breaking up. Are they right?
Stuck in Curitiba
J:
Dear Stuck,
First of all, a heart to heart after twelve years is a step in the right direction, not a sign of the end. Long relationships often go through periods of monotony, and that doesn't mean the love is gone. Sometimes the root of the problem is simple: one or both partners stopped pursuing their own dreams.
A planned pause can work, but only if you are both upfront about it. Before you go, sit down together and agree on the practical things: money, how often you'll call, and an end date. Ask him to tell you honestly how he feels, and don't ask him to pretend he's happy if he isn't. If jealousy is already a problem, a break will probably make it worse.
Your husband asked you what you wanted. To me, that shows he cares about your happiness. Three months is a short time in twelve years. And while you're in Lisbon, he could take a breather too. Maybe there's something he only gets to do once in a blue moon.
So my advice is: go, call often, and come back ready for a new chapter, together.
Jo
